summary: No reachable vulnerability. Trust boundary unchanged: createHand still validates stakes (positive safe integers, A-4 10 x minimumStack bound), deck, seats and stacks (Number.isSafeInteger); the floor only drops from minimumStack to bigBlind + 1, and the TASK-1.31 total-stacks <= MAX_SAFE_INTEGER check is untouched and still runs after the per-seat check. Because chips are conserved, every stack, contribution, pot, award and the new result.returned amount stays at or below that total, so all stay safe integers. Conservation: gather puts collected - back into the pot and adds back to the top bettor's stack (net zero). back = top - second street contribution is >= 0 and <= that seat's contribution, so no chips are created; ties give back = 0. The call amount min(owe, stack) comes only from legalActions and applyAction accepts only exact legal actions, so stacks cannot go negative. allIn is derived (stack - added === 0), never taken from input. No player is ever chosen to act while all-in, and with open.length <= 1 the hand runs out (D-7) using the same D-5 deck positions, so dealing fairness is unchanged. Invariants C3/C4 now subtract returned and the new C5 recomputes it independently, which strengthens the check rather than loosening it. Runner change is reporting only. No new dependencies, I/O, randomness or deserialization (no JSON.parse/localStorage in src). Note for TASK-3.10: once restored sessions feed HandState into applyAction without going through createHand, allIn/stack/contribution fields become untrusted and need re-validation (e.g. checkState) at that boundary. Accepted A-1 (a short all-in can win the whole single pot until TASK-1.10) is a correctness limitation that conserves chips, already tracked, so not a security finding. Ran the five relevant engine/table test files and all 19 tests passed.
